passages.text: And the LORD said to Moses, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them that if a man or woman makes a special vow, the vow of a Nazirite, to separate himself to the LORD, he is to abstain from wine and strong drink. He must not drink vinegar made from wine or strong drink, and he must not drink any grape juice or eat fresh grapes or raisins.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to the Israelites.
The LORD told Moses to give the Israelites instructions.
A man or a woman may make a special vow.
This vow is called the vow of a Nazirite.
A Nazirite separates himself or herself to the LORD.
A Nazirite must not drink wine.
A Nazirite must not drink strong drink.
A Nazirite must not drink vinegar made from wine.
A Nazirite must not drink vinegar made from strong drink.
A Nazirite must not drink any grape juice.
A Nazirite must not eat fresh grapes.
A Nazirite must not eat raisins.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּר֙ אֶל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֲלֵהֶ֑ם אִ֣ישׁ אֽוֹ־ אִשָּׁ֗ה כִּ֤י יַפְלִא֙ לִנְדֹּר֙ נֶ֣דֶר נָזִ֔יר לְהַזִּ֖יר לַֽיהוָֽה׃ מִיַּ֤יִן וְשֵׁכָר֙ יַזִּ֔יר חֹ֥מֶץ יַ֛יִן וְחֹ֥מֶץ שֵׁכָ֖ר לֹ֣א יִשְׁתֶּ֑ה וְכָל־ מִשְׁרַ֤ת עֲנָבִים֙ לֹ֣א יִשְׁתֶּ֔ה וַעֲנָבִ֛ים לַחִ֥ים וִיבֵשִׁ֖ים לֹ֥א יֹאכֵֽל׃

passages.text: All the days of his separation, he is not to eat anything that comes from the grapevine, not even the seeds or skins.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a man or woman who makes a special vow to separate himself or herself to the LORD.
During the days of a Nazirite’s separation, he or she must not eat anything from the grapevine.
He or she must not eat grape seeds.
He or she must not eat grape skins.
passages.original: כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֑וֹ מִכֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יֵעָשֶׂ֜ה מִגֶּ֣פֶן הַיַּ֗יִן מֵחַרְצַנִּ֛ים וְעַד־ זָ֖ג לֹ֥א יֹאכֵֽל׃

passages.text: For the entire period of his vow of separation, no razor shall pass over his head. He must be holy until the time of his separation to the LORD is complete; he must let the hair of his head grow long.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a man or woman who makes a special vow to separate himself to the LORD.
During the entire time of his vow, the Nazirite must not cut his hair.
No razor may touch his head.
He must remain holy until his time of separation to the LORD is finished.
He must let the hair on his head grow long.
passages.original: כָּל־ יְמֵי֙ נֶ֣דֶר נִזְר֔וֹ תַּ֖עַר לֹא־ יַעֲבֹ֣ר עַל־ רֹאשׁ֑וֹ עַד־ מְלֹ֨את הַיָּמִ֜ם אֲשֶׁר־ יַזִּ֤יר לַיהוָה֙ קָדֹ֣שׁ יִהְיֶ֔ה גַּדֵּ֥ל פֶּ֖רַע שְׂעַ֥ר רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: Throughout the days of his separation to the LORD, he must not go near a dead body.
passages.sermon: A Nazirite is a person who makes a vow of separation to the LORD.\r\nDuring all the days of his separation, he must not go near a dead body.
passages.original: כָּל־ יְמֵ֥י הַזִּיר֖וֹ לַיהוָ֑ה עַל־ נֶ֥פֶשׁ מֵ֖ת לֹ֥א יָבֹֽא׃

passages.text: Even if his father or mother or brother or sister should die, he is not to defile himself, because the crown of consecration to his God is upon his head.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a vow of separation to the LORD.
The Nazirite must not defile himself for anyone who dies.
This rule includes his father.
This rule includes his mother.
This rule includes his brother.
This rule includes his sister.
He must not defile himself for them if they die.
The reason is that the crown of consecration to his God is on his head.
passages.original: לְאָבִ֣יו וּלְאִמּ֗וֹ לְאָחִיו֙ וּלְאַ֣חֹת֔וֹ לֹא־ יִטַּמָּ֥א לָהֶ֖ם בְּמֹתָ֑ם כִּ֛י נֵ֥זֶר אֱלֹהָ֖יו עַל־ רֹאשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: Throughout the time of his separation, he is holy to the LORD.
passages.sermon: A Nazirite is a person who makes a vow to separate himself to the LORD.\r\nDuring all the days of his vow, the Nazirite must remain set apart.\r\nHe is holy to the LORD for the entire time of his separation.
passages.original: כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֑וֹ קָדֹ֥שׁ ה֖וּא לַֽיהוָֽה׃

passages.text: If someone suddenly dies in his presence and defiles his consecrated head of hair, he must shave his head on the day of his cleansing—the seventh day.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a special vow to God.
A Nazirite must keep himself holy to the LORD.
If a person dies suddenly in the Nazirite’s presence, this makes the Nazirite’s consecrated hair unclean.
This defiles the Nazirite’s head.
The Nazirite must become clean again.
On the seventh day, which is the day of his cleansing, the Nazirite must shave his head.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יָמ֨וּת מֵ֤ת עָלָיו֙ בְּפֶ֣תַע פִּתְאֹ֔ם וְטִמֵּ֖א רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑וֹ וְגִלַּ֤ח רֹאשׁוֹ֙ בְּי֣וֹם טָהֳרָת֔וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֖י יְגַלְּחֶֽנּוּ׃

passages.text: On the eighth day he must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a special vow to the LORD.
He separates himself for a time.
If a Nazirite becomes defiled by a sudden death near him, he must be cleansed.
On the eighth day after his cleansing, the Nazirite must bring two birds.
He must bring either two turtledoves or two young pigeons.
He must bring them to the priest.
He must go to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
passages.original: וּבַיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁמִינִ֗י יָבִא֙ שְׁתֵּ֣י תֹרִ֔ים א֥וֹ שְׁנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יוֹנָ֑ה אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶל־ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃

passages.text: And the priest is to offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to make atonement for him, because he has sinned by being in the presence of the dead body. On that day he must consecrate his head again.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a special vow to the LORD.
The Nazirite must avoid contact with dead bodies.
If a Nazirite becomes defiled by being in the presence of a dead body, he has sinned.
The priest must take two birds from the Nazirite.
The priest offers one bird as a sin offering.
The priest offers the other bird as a burnt offering.
The priest makes atonement for the Nazirite.
The atonement is for the Nazirite’s sin of being near a dead body.
On that same day, the Nazirite must consecrate his head again.
passages.original: וְעָשָׂ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֶחָ֤ד לְחַטָּאת֙ וְאֶחָ֣ד לְעֹלָ֔ה וְכִפֶּ֣ר עָלָ֔יו מֵאֲשֶׁ֥ר חָטָ֖א עַל־ הַנָּ֑פֶשׁ וְקִדַּ֥שׁ אֶת־ רֹאשׁ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

passages.text: He must rededicate his time of separation to the LORD and bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering. But the preceding days shall not be counted, because his separation was defiled.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a special vow to the LORD.
He must separate himself from certain things for a set time.
If a Nazirite becomes defiled during this time, he must start over.
He must rededicate his days of separation to the LORD.
He must bring a year-old male lamb as a guilt offering.
The days he completed before do not count.
His earlier time of separation was defiled.
passages.original: וְהִזִּ֤יר לַֽיהוָה֙ אֶת־ יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔וֹ וְהֵבִ֛יא כֶּ֥בֶשׂ בֶּן־ שְׁנָת֖וֹ לְאָשָׁ֑ם וְהַיָּמִ֤ים הָרִאשֹׁנִים֙ יִפְּל֔וּ כִּ֥י טָמֵ֖א נִזְרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Now this is the law of the Nazirite when his time of separation is complete: He must be brought to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, and he is to present an offering to the LORD of an unblemished year-old male lamb as a burnt offering, an unblemished year-old female lamb as a sin offering, and an unblemished ram as a peace offering— together with their grain offerings and drink offerings—and a basket of unleavened cakes made from fine flour mixed with oil and unleavened wafers coated with oil.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a special vow to the LORD.
The Nazirite separates himself from certain things for a set time.
When the Nazirite completes his time of separation, he must follow this law.
He must go to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
He must bring his offerings to the LORD.
He must offer a male lamb that is one year old and has no defect.
This male lamb is for a burnt offering.
He must offer a female lamb that is one year old and has no defect.
This female lamb is for a sin offering.
He must offer a ram that has no defect.
This ram is for a peace offering.
He must also bring a basket of unleavened bread.
The basket must have cakes made from fine flour mixed with oil.
The basket must also have unleavened wafers spread with oil.
He must bring the grain offerings and drink offerings that go with them.
passages.original: וְזֹ֥את תּוֹרַ֖ת הַנָּזִ֑יר בְּי֗וֹם מְלֹאת֙ יְמֵ֣י נִזְר֔וֹ יָבִ֣יא אֹת֔וֹ אֶל־ פֶּ֖תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵֽד׃ וְהִקְרִ֣יב אֶת־ קָרְבָּנ֣וֹ לַיהוָ֡ה כֶּבֶשׂ֩ בֶּן־ שְׁנָת֨וֹ תָמִ֤ים אֶחָד֙ לְעֹלָ֔ה וְכַבְשָׂ֨ה אַחַ֧ת בַּת־ שְׁנָתָ֛הּ תְּמִימָ֖ה לְחַטָּ֑את וְאַֽיִל־ אֶחָ֥ד תָּמִ֖ים לִשְׁלָמִֽים׃ וְסַ֣ל מַצּ֗וֹת סֹ֤לֶת חַלֹּת֙ בְּלוּלֹ֣ת בַּשֶּׁ֔מֶן וּרְקִיקֵ֥י מַצּ֖וֹת מְשֻׁחִ֣ים בַּשָּׁ֑מֶן וּמִנְחָתָ֖ם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: The priest is to present all these before the LORD and make the sin offering and the burnt offering.
passages.sermon:
The priest stands before the LORD.
The priest presents all the offerings.
The priest makes the sin offering.
The priest makes the burnt offering.
passages.original: וְהִקְרִ֥יב הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה וְעָשָׂ֥ה אֶת־ חַטָּאת֖וֹ וְאֶת־ עֹלָתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He shall also offer the ram as a peace offering to the LORD, along with the basket of unleavened bread. And the priest is to offer the accompanying grain offering and drink offering.
passages.sermon:
The Nazirite must offer a ram.
The ram is a peace offering to the LORD.
He must also bring a basket of unleavened bread.
The priest must offer the grain offering with the ram.
The priest must also offer the drink offering.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ הָאַ֜יִל יַעֲשֶׂ֨ה זֶ֤בַח שְׁלָמִים֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה עַ֖ל סַ֣ל הַמַּצּ֑וֹת וְעָשָׂה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן אֶת־ מִנְחָת֖וֹ וְאֶת־ נִסְכּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Then at the entrance to the Tent of Meeting, the Nazirite is to shave his consecrated head, take the hair, and put it on the fire under the peace offering.
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a special vow to the LORD.
The Nazirite must go to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.
The Nazirite must shave his consecrated head there.
He must take the hair from his head.
He must put the hair on the fire.
The fire is under the peace offering.
passages.original: וְגִלַּ֣ח הַנָּזִ֗יר פֶּ֛תַח אֹ֥הֶל מוֹעֵ֖ד אֶת־ רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֑וֹ וְלָקַ֗ח אֶת־ שְׂעַר֙ רֹ֣אשׁ נִזְר֔וֹ וְנָתַן֙ עַל־ הָאֵ֔שׁ אֲשֶׁר־ תַּ֖חַת זֶ֥בַח הַשְּׁלָמִֽים׃

passages.text: And the priest is to take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened cake from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put them into the hands of the Nazirite who has just shaved the hair of his consecration.
passages.sermon:
The priest takes the boiled shoulder from the ram.
The priest takes one unleavened cake from the basket.
The priest takes one unleavened wafer.
The Nazirite has just shaved the hair of his consecration.
The priest puts the boiled shoulder, the cake, and the wafer into the hands of the Nazirite.
passages.original: וְלָקַ֨ח הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־ הַזְּרֹ֣עַ בְּשֵׁלָה֮ מִן־ הָאַיִל֒ וְֽחַלַּ֨ת מַצָּ֤ה אַחַת֙ מִן־ הַסַּ֔ל וּרְקִ֥יק מַצָּ֖ה אֶחָ֑ד וְנָתַן֙ עַל־ כַּפֵּ֣י הַנָּזִ֔יר אַחַ֖ר הִֽתְגַּלְּח֥וֹ אֶת־ נִזְרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The priest shall then wave them as a wave offering before the LORD. This is a holy portion for the priest, in addition to the breast of the wave offering and the thigh that was presented. After that, the Nazirite may drink wine.
passages.sermon:
The priest takes the items.
The priest waves them before the LORD as a wave offering.
These items are holy for the priest.
They are in addition to the breast of the wave offering.
They are also in addition to the thigh that was presented.
After this, the Nazirite may drink wine.
passages.original: וְהֵנִיף֩ אוֹתָ֨ם הַכֹּהֵ֥ן׀ תְּנוּפָה֮ לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ קֹ֤דֶשׁ הוּא֙ לַכֹּהֵ֔ן עַ֚ל חֲזֵ֣ה הַתְּנוּפָ֔ה וְעַ֖ל שׁ֣וֹק הַתְּרוּמָ֑ה וְאַחַ֛ר יִשְׁתֶּ֥ה הַנָּזִ֖יר יָֽיִן׃

passages.text: This is the law of the Nazirite who vows his offering to the LORD for his separation, in addition to whatever else he can afford; he must fulfill whatever vow he makes, according to the law of his separation.”
passages.sermon:
A Nazirite is a person who makes a special vow to the LORD.
The Nazirite separates himself for God.
This is the law for the Nazirite.
The Nazirite must bring his offering to the LORD for his separation.
He must also bring anything else he can afford.
He must do everything he promised in his vow.
He must follow the law for Nazirites.
passages.original: זֹ֣את תּוֹרַ֣ת הַנָּזִיר֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדֹּר֒ קָרְבָּנ֤וֹ לַֽיהוָה֙ עַל־ נִזְר֔וֹ מִלְּבַ֖ד אֲשֶׁר־ תַּשִּׂ֣יג יָד֑וֹ כְּפִ֤י נִדְרוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר יִדֹּ֔ר כֵּ֣ן יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה עַ֖ל תּוֹרַ֥ת נִזְרֽוֹ׃פ

passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Tell Aaron and his sons: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them: ‘May the LORD bless you and keep you; may the LORD cause His face to shine upon you and be gracious to you; may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace.’
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses.
The LORD gave Moses a command.
The LORD told Moses to speak to Aaron and his sons.
Aaron and his sons were the priests of Israel.
The LORD said, “This is how you must bless the Israelites.
Say these words to them:
‘May the LORD bless you.
May the LORD keep you.
May the LORD make His face shine on you.
May the LORD be gracious to you.
May the LORD lift up His face toward you.
May the LORD give you peace.’”
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃ דַּבֵּ֤ר אֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹן֙ וְאֶל־ בָּנָ֣יו לֵאמֹ֔ר כֹּ֥ה תְבָרֲכ֖וּ אֶת־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אָמ֖וֹר לָהֶֽם׃ס יְבָרֶכְךָ֥ יְהוָ֖ה וְיִשְׁמְרֶֽךָ׃ס יָאֵ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה׀ פָּנָ֛יו אֵלֶ֖יךָ וִֽיחֻנֶּֽךָּ׃ס יִשָּׂ֨א יְהוָ֤ה׀ פָּנָיו֙ אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְיָשֵׂ֥ם לְךָ֖ שָׁלֽוֹם׃ס

passages.text: So they shall put My name on the Israelites, and I will bless them.”
passages.sermon:
God spoke to Moses.
God gave instructions to Aaron and his sons.
God told them to bless the Israelites.
God said, “Place My name on the Israelites.”
God promised, “I will bless them.”
passages.original: וְשָׂמ֥וּ אֶת־ שְׁמִ֖י עַל־ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַאֲנִ֖י אֲבָרֲכֵֽם׃פ
